title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
slides: Can Anthropic's Claude Duet outplay Muse at its own game?
A new AI agent built for hands-on creative work
But early tests show it stalls on multi-step projects
Teams can now assign it whole workflows, not prompts
Try one real project before your competitor does
thread_text:
1. Claude Duet vs Muse

Anthropic's new agent is designed for hands-on creative work. Early tests reveal it stalls on multi-step projects, raising doubts about its readiness.

2. Built for Creatives

Duet lets teams assign entire workflows, not just prompts. That shift could redefine how creative work gets delegated to AI.

3. Stalls on Complexity

When projects require multiple steps, Duet struggles. This limitation might frustrate teams expecting seamless execution.

4. Workflows, Not Prompts

Assigning whole workflows means AI handles sequences, not isolated tasks. But if it stalls, the promise of end-to-end automation weakens.

5. Test Before Rivals

Try one real project with Duet this week. Does it save time or create more editing? Share your experience.

instagram.caption:
Anthropic's new Claude Duet is built to handle entire creative workflows, not just single prompts. 🤖

That means teams can hand it a whole sequence of tasks instead of typing each step.

But early tests show it stalls on multi-step projects, so end-to-end automation doesn't fully hold up yet.

If you're assigning real work to it, expect to step in and fix things mid-project rather than set it and forget it. 🛠️

Would you trust Duet with one full project this week, or wait to see if it stalls first?
